transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-06
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Redwood: Priya Desai (AE), Liam Chen (SE), Ruth Park (CSM)
- Customer: Mara Patel (Head of ML Ops), Diego Alvarez (Platform Eng), Samir Rao (Finance), Nina Kaur (Security)

Summary: Quarterly operational pulse. Short review of current usage, cost anomalies, one-off tail-latency events in September, and planning for an October pilot to validate reserved capacity + burst settings.

---
00:00 Priya Desai: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. can we do quick intros? this is a short QBR-ish pulse.
00:14 Mara Patel: Hi, Mara here, ML Ops. we've got a couple folks from platform and finance. thanks.
00:20 Diego Alvarez: Diego, platform eng, we'll be looking at autoscale and infra side.
00:25 Samir Rao: Samir, finance, i'll be watching the unit economics.
00:30 Priya Desai: Great. Liam from our infra team?
00:33 Liam Chen: Yup hey all. i primarily looked at the september tail issue, and i brought a couple logs.
00:40 Ruth Park: Ruth, CSM, just here to track actions and help coordinate the pilot.
00:45 [00:45]
01:02 Priya Desai: Quick status — usage is up 28% month over month, tokens per minute spiked after the new recommendation model rolled out. that's mostly good but it pushed you into burst territory on 9/22 and 9/29. we flagged a couple tail-latency events around 350-450ms above expected.
01:25 Mara Patel: yeah the 9/22 incident was visible in our dashboards — some inference calls where KV cache didn't hit. we suspect a cold-start pattern on some shards.
01:38 Liam Chen: from our logs, it looked like prefix/cache warmup was uneven. there was also an interleaving with retries from your app causing request duplication, which magnified latency.
01:50 Diego Alvarez: can you explain 'KV cash' — i read it as K V cash in the notes, heh.
01:56 Liam Chen: (laughs) it's KV cache — key value cache for the transformer kv store. transcription sometimes makes odd splits.
02:05 Samir Rao: cost question first — when you say burst territory, are we billed at on-demand rate or do we get any smoothing from reserved? our bill this month was about 18% above forecast.
02:18 Priya Desai: short answer: reserved capacity covers baseline throughput; burst is billed at a higher rate. but we can propose a burst cap policy and a blended pricing tier to smooth surprises. we'll share numbers in the follow up.
02:31 Samir Rao: okay need that by Friday ideally.
02:35 Priya Desai: noted.
02:40 [02:40]
02:58 Mara Patel: On reliability, the number one ask from our execs is tail percentiles — 95th and 99th because customer-facing features are sensitive. do you have a recommendation on SLO thresholds?
03:12 Liam Chen: yes, recommended SLO is p95 < 120ms for cached hits, and p99 < 300ms for hot paths. for cold paths we typically aim for p95 < 250ms. that's a rough baseline.
03:27 Diego Alvarez: the 9/29 spike hit p99 at about 760ms for a 5 minute window which triggered our alerting.
03:35 Liam Chen: right, that came from two correlated events: 1) a cache flush due to model reload; 2) a storm of parallel requests from a batch job that retried on 503s.
03:46 Mara Patel: the model reloads — are those rolling restarts or full model re-inits?
03:53 Liam Chen: looks like a full reload on a subset of instances when we triggered a canary roll — the canary didn't warm the cache as expected. we can propose a canary warmup sequence so reloads don't evict critical prefix cache.
04:08 Priya Desai: Actionable idea: for the pilot we can do a canary + warmup + traffic mirroring for 24-48 hours and measure tail. That will reduce exposure.
04:20 Mara Patel: sounds good.
04:24 [04:24]
04:40 Samir Rao: on the pricing model — curious about dedicated vs hosted. if we move to a small dedicated pool for the recommendation model, what are break-even points?
04:52 Priya Desai: we ran a sim earlier — at your average sustained qps the break-even is around 25% sustained increase over baseline. with your current growth trajectory you hit that in roughly 6-8 weeks. but we can design a reserved + burst hybrid for cost governance.
05:09 Samir Rao: can you put the sim numbers in a spreadsheet? i want per-token cost and effective hourly spend.
05:15 Priya Desai: yes, will share.
05:18 Diego Alvarez: curious about autoscale settings — we've seen your autoscaler spin up GPUs but sometimes the placement latency kills throughput. any suggestions?
05:30 Liam Chen: suggestion is to set a higher min-replicas for peak windows so placement is pre-warmed, and also use regional placement affinity to keep warm instances in the same AZ. if you're on private deployment we can also recommend node-prep scripts to reduce GPU init time.
05:50 Mara Patel: we're on hosted today but considering private for compliance. what are the KPI tradeoffs?
05:57 Priya Desai: private gives you network and data isolation plus KMS control, but you trade some of the managed autoscale niceties and need ops bandwidth. we provide an on-prem package with orchestration and automated kernel selection but you'll need someone for the infra side.
06:15 Nina Kaur: a security note — we need SOC2 evidence plus explicit customer-managed KMS integration. also we'd like audit logs forwarded to our Splunk.
06:27 Ruth Park: we can compile a compliance packet. Priya, Liam, can you own the KMS+audit log answers?
06:33 Priya Desai: yes we'll send the packet and a sample audit log schema.
06:36 [06:36]
06:50 Diego Alvarez: for the pilot scope — i'd like to test two endpoints: recs-v2 (heavy context, long seq len) and classify-lite (short context). run them under 50% of real traffic with mirrored requests for two weeks.
07:05 Liam Chen: good plan — recs-v2 will stress KV cache and long sequence kernels, classify-lite will exercise batching efficiency. we'll instrument sample latency heatmaps.
07:18 Mara Patel: what's success criteria? p95 within 1.2x of baseline and cost per 1k requests under X?
07:26 Priya Desai: propose success: p95 degradation <= 20% vs baseline, p99 improved by at least 10% after warmup strategies, and cost delta <= 8% with reserved+burst configuration. open to tune the numbers.
07:42 Samir Rao: finance will insist on an explicit cost cap in the pilot otherwise it looks risky.
07:49 Priya Desai: fair. we'll include a hard spending cap and alerts at 60/80/100%.
07:56 [07:56]
08:10 Mara Patel: about routing — can we route low-priority ops to cheaper model variants automatically?
08:17 Liam Chen: yes, smart routing policy supports model variants and region-based routing. you can set priority tags on requests and a fallback to cheaper quantized variants when load is high.
08:29 Diego Alvarez: any concerns about quality when we fallback to quantized models? we've got customers that are sensitive to hallucinations.
08:36 Priya Desai: we include evals tied to prompt sets to detect drift. Recommend running shadow evals for a week to measure quality deltas before letting fallback auto-route.
08:49 Mara Patel: please include a sample eval harness.
08:52 Liam Chen: will attach a small harness and a sample prompt suite.
08:57 [08:57]
09:12 Nina Kaur: on the KMS side — does Redwood support external HSM providers or just cloud KMS?
09:20 Priya Desai: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, and external HSM via an enterprise integration. we'll add specifics in the compliance packet.
09:31 Nina Kaur: also need encrypted at rest proof and key rotation cadence.
09:36 Ruth Park: we'll include key rotation docs, and an example rotation policy.
09:40 [09:40]
09:55 Samir Rao: how often do these cache warmup improvements actually reduce monthly bill vs. just pushing costs to the next month?
10:03 Liam Chen: if cache hit rate improves by 10-15% on your heavy endpoints, tokenized cost can drop by up to 12% for that traffic. It's not purely deferred cost; it's improved efficiency.
10:15 Mara Patel: ok, so concrete deliverables from Redwood are: pricing spreadsheet, benchmark script + logs, compliance packet, eval harness, and a pilot plan with SLOs and hard cost cap.
10:27 Priya Desai: correct — we'll deliver those within the next week window.
10:32 [10:32]
10:48 Diego Alvarez: small nit — can we do a quick on-call playbook for if there is another tail event? who do we call?
10:56 Priya Desai: yes, we'll include an on-call runbook and contacts. for the pilot we'll schedule a weekly sync and a rapid-response channel.
11:06 Mara Patel: excellent.
11:10 [11:10]
11:28 Priya Desai: let's recap next steps: Priya sends pricing + burst policy (due 10/09), Liam sends benchmark script and initial logs (due 10/08), Ruth to set up pilot calendar invite and Slack channel, Nina to send compliance must-haves, Mara to confirm pilot endpoints and traffic mix by 10/13.
11:48 Mara Patel: confirming; we'll prioritize the recs-v2 and classify-lite endpoints for the mirrored test.
11:55 Priya Desai: thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and schedule.
12:00 Meeting end.
